msItem.title: Bible
Septuagint, New Testament, Epistle of Barnabas, Shepherd of Hermas

condition.p: The manuscript is partly lost. Some pages are incomplete.

layout.p: Most of the manuscript is in four columns.
Poetic books of Septuagint in two columns.

decoDesc.p: Black ink, with red ink for some headings and numbering systems

surrogates.p: Black and white facsimile by H. and K. Lake, 1911 and 1922. Colour digital images taken by the Codex Sinaiticus Project team in 2006-2009. Images online at http://www.codexsinaiticus.org/en/manuscript.aspx

projectDesc.p: This transcription was made by the Codex Sinaiticus Project as part of an online presentation and edition of Codex Sinaiticus between 2002 and 2010.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription covers the whole manuscript. Base texts used: Nestle-Aland, Novum Testamentum graece, 27th edition. Double-transcribed from digital images taken by the Codex Sinaiticus Project team in 2006-2009, supplied by the Codex Sinaiticus Project. Verified against the manuscript portions in Leipzig, St Petersburg and Moscow in 2008-2009.
The transcription includes foliation, lineation, all punctuation and abbreviations.

The initial transcription file was a plain text file for use with COLLATE, later converted to XML. The XML is based on the TEI P5 guidelines, although there are some innovations in order to represent the physical layout of each page. In particular, pb cb and lb elements are divided into corresponding opening and closing elements, with an additional margin element inside these elements containing marginal material.
Further information about the procedures followed may be found in the electronic edition

The main piece of text (from the ϲ onwards) is straightforward. The difficult area is the letters partially extant earlier in the line. They are consonant with the reading Αρνων η: the first stroke would be the right vertical of ν, then a space (the dark mark between them is unlikely to be ink), then the top left of η, followed by a hole into which ε would fit. The reading Αροηρ is very improbable.
